rows.evidence: The declared class in libs/bytepacking/Packet.h is jag::PacketT, instantiated with a byte Array. Compiler-recovered callers such as Js5ResourceProvider take PacketT<Array<unsigned char>>. The original assertion in GaiaConnection.cpp uses Packet::SMALL and PacketT diagnostics display Packet, documenting the source-facing shorthand. The 530 byte array and cursor correspond to m_data and m_pos. CoordFine.h and PlayerData.h retain the byte-offset expressions for alternate readers. For four-byte input at offsets 0..3, g4_alt2 forms 2:3:0:1 and g4_alt3 forms 1:0:3:2 in most significant byte order. Packet.h and HardwareInfo.h retain their inverse writers. PacketJ supplies the MSB-first gMidiVarLen/pMidiVarLen and gSmartsExtend (clientbuild.h). PacketT's gVarInt reads the first seven bits as the least significant group. The plain JagString reader/writer copy the underlying bytes, as gStringNoConversion/pStringNoConversion do. SD keeps its terminator argument, separate nullable and versioned JagString reads, reverse buffer read, and CRC append. The little-endian signed add-halfword and unsigned little-endian three-byte read lack independently recovered implementation symbols. SD byte access, exception timing, permutations and string behavior are covered in test/packet.test.ts.

rows.evidence: An LRU entry node (extends jf, fields row u and slot s) that only the procedural-texture monochrome row cache wk uses. osclient-nxt has no procedural texture row caches, and generic jtl LRUCache entries are templates, not this class. No counterpart.

ld.run() is the audio pump. Every ~10 ms it calls dg.a(false) (the player service) on each registered PcmPlayer. In NXT, PCMPlayer::SetInput spawns a PlayerTask(PCMPlayer&), a MixerWorker task with SetInterval(1). Its OnInterval does SetWorkerThread(); player->Service() (the pure slot 6); ClearWorkerThread(). PCMPlayer::GetPlayer(id, size) rejects player id > 1 ('invalid player id'), which mirrors ld.l = new dg[2] and the slot check in lg.a. Difference: NXT runs one task per player, while ld is one thread with two slots. The moved statics (size-2 route finder, sprite-group lookup, display-mode byte) have no place here. The NXT PCMPlayer::PlayerTask drives one bound player. The 530 Runnable services two slots and pumps Signlink events. Use the exact nested short type name.

le is the abstract wheel interface. It exists only so that ih can be loaded reflectively on pre-1.4 JVMs. NXT has no separate interface. Its three abstract methods (poll-and-reset, attach, detach) line up with ClientMouseListener::GetAndResetWheelRotation, Init and Destroy, so it folds into the same class as ih and uk. Keep the current name. Its many statics (actor turning, login state machine, point-in-triangle, decor removal) are unrelated.

lf is a Java InputStream whose read() sleeps 30 s and returns -1. se.c(3) swaps it in for ::breakcon. osclient-nxt has no stream stand-in class: the index has no Broken/InputStream classes. The C++ equivalent of breakcon is ClientStream::Drop(), which closes the socket and sets the status to 0 (called by Js5WorkerThread::DropClientConnection and the clientdrop console command); it does not use a substitute stream. The large drawInterface static is a moved static and does not decide the class's name. Keep the current name.

530 lg uses op1 input type, op2 output type, op3 default string, op4 default int, and op5/op6 g2 count then g4 key -> string or int in a hashtable. It also builds a reverse table lazily for contains-value queries. RT5 EnumType::DecodeType has the same layout: 1 -> field_56 (input type), 2 -> m_outputType, 3 -> field_104 default string, 4 -> field_72 default int, 5/6 -> g2 count of g4 key -> VarValue into hash_map field_136. Its BuildOptionsReverse/GetReverseLookup fill the reverse map field_224 lazily, as lg.c(B)/lg.d(B) build B for lg.a(ZLid;)Z and lg.d(II)Z. oldscape EnumType stores the entries in parallel arrays (m_numOptions) and has no reverse lookup, so it is structurally further away.
rows.alternative: jag::oldscape::configdecoder::EnumType (libs/oldscape/rs2lib/configdecoder/EnumType.h)

Oldscape SpotType::Decode(packet,code) uses the same opcodes and encodings: 1 model g2 (field_4), 2 anim g2 (field_8, default -1), 4/5 resize g2 (field_112/116, default 128), 6 angle g2 (field_120), 7 ambient g1 (field_124), 8 contrast g1 (field_128), 40 recolour pairs, 41 retexture pairs. GetBaseModel lights with (ambient+64, contrast+850, -30,-50,-30) and caches the result in m_modelCache. GetTempModel2 animates through SeqType when anim != -1 && frame != -1, otherwise copies; scales when not 128; rotates for 90/180/270. That is li.E line for line (m.O = m_modelCache, r.V = m_recentUse). The only extra in 530 is op 9 (f=true). RT5 EffectAnimType has the same op 9 as its hill-rotate flag (ShouldHillRotate: field_176==3), and 530 reads li.f in bk/pb to apply actor hill tilt to the spot model. RT5 still names the concept 'spot' (Js5ConfigGroup::SPOTTYPE, Js5Archive::JS5_CONFIG_SPOT, which is 530's archive 21).
rows.alternative: jag::game::EffectAnimType (libs/game/runetek5/config/effectanimtype/EffectAnimType.h): the later RT5/NXT rename. It has the same op 1/2/4-8/40/41 layout plus op 9 hill-rotate, but its fields became floats and materials.

rows.evidence: Static-only obfuscator bucket. Its dominant member decodes the server reflection-check request (Class.forName, getDeclaredField/Method) into a qj node. MidiFile::PatchNoteSet is a nested class of MidiFile: 16 bytes, which is a std::bitset<128>, one bit per MIDI note. MidiFile holds an eastl::hash_map<int, PatchNoteSet> keyed by program, and Patch::LoadWaves(WaveCache&, std::bitset<128>&, ErrorCapture&) loads only the samples whose notes are set. lk is the same: the 128-entry note-used byte[] in ee's (MidiFile) nc keyed by program, set on note-on and passed to tg.a(...) (Patch) so it loads only the needed samples. ee allocates the 128-note mask per patch and ng passes it to sample loading; the nested MidiFile::PatchNoteSet holds that mask in the NXT caller.

WaveCache(Js5& jagfx, Js5& vorbis) is ll(al synth, al vorbis), and both hold node hash maps keyed by long long. WaveCache::HashAudioID(group, file, isVorbis) = (group<<16 | (group>>12 | (group&4095)<<4) ^ file), XORed with 0x100000000 for Vorbis. That is the exact ll key formula. GetJagFx(int,int,Array<int>& budget) and GetJagVorbis(int,int,Array<int>&) are the private per-group/file loaders. The public GetJagFx/GetJagVorbis(int id, Array<int>&, ...) choose group or file the same way ll.a(I[II) and ll.a(II[I) do. Verified 530 member spellings against libs/oldscape/jagex3/sound/wavecache.cpp. The two archive group/file overloads perform distinct cache-key and JagFX/JagVorbis reads. Their single-ID overloads choose group 0 or file 0 from archive capacity. The TS group/file forms have suffix 2 to retain four separate Java method bodies.

m is the decoded script data class. ClientScript::DecodeScript fills the same layout: name, opcode array, int operands, string operands, four g2 counts (int/string locals, int/string args = m.E/I/K/R in that order) and the switch tables (m.N). It is cached in a 128-entry LRUHashCache, as m is cached in sf.g = vj(128). RT5 jag::game::ClientScript adds long locals and is the farther match, but its accessors name the local counts.
rows.alternative: jag::game::ClientScript (libs/game/runetek5/script/ClientScript.h)

rows.evidence: The oldscape QuickGround(int×6, bool, bool) is 28 bytes: four corner colours, texture, rgb (field_0), and the flat bool (field_24). 530 ma(int×6, boolean) has the same 6 ints + flat (sw/se/ne/nw colour, texture, minimap rgb, flat). NXT only adds a second bool. Both are built by the flat-tile path of SetGround (530 uk.java:186/206, flat = all four heights equal) and stored in the Square's quick-ground slot (530 ra.F, NXT Square+48 'qg'). Oldscape has no BAS. RT5 BASType::DecodeType('.bas', config group Js5ConfigGroup::BASTYPE = 32, the same group as 530) uses the same opcode skeleton. op1 reads two anims (field_56 = ready, used by GetReadyAnim, then m_walkForward); ops 2-9 are single anims; op26 reads two g1<<2 values (m_hillRotateWidth/Length, 530 w/j = g1*4); ops 38-42 are single anims; 43/44/45 are later anims and overlay height, which 530 reads and drops. NXT skips 530's ops 27-37 (the slot transform matrix and turn/roll/pitch tuning), so those are 530-only fields. NXT adds ops 46-56 (crawl/run/walk turns, random ready list). Opcode-matched names disagree with some current TS names: op2-5 are 'slow*' in TS but crawl* in NXT, and ops 38/39 are 'turnRight/turnLeft' in TS but m_readyTurnLeft/m_readyTurnRight in NXT.

rows.evidence: mi is a final Node (extends jf) with three instance ints: s = map-function id (LocType jb.j), F = x, z = y. The 530 world-map region decode (sj.b) pushes one mi per loc with a map function into the list rf.v. The overview (oc.a) iterates rf.v and draws flashing 4x4 boxes for entries matching the flashed id, and the region renderer (e.a) uses mi to defer flashing icons. The RT5 world map in libs/game/runetek5/scene/worldmap/WorldMap.cpp descends directly from this code. Unrelated statics also live here: mi.a(IIII)I is the HSL 24-to-16 packer with stepped saturation halving above lightness 179/192/217/243, used by the world-map underlay blend in og; mi.a(BJ)id is base-37 decode. rows.evidence: The NXT ctor ClientLocAnim(int,int,int,int,int,int,int seq,bool random,shared_ptr<ModelSource> prev,int loopCycle) has the same parameter order as ml(L locId, o shape, s angle, j level, A x, y z, seq, boolean randomStart, ug prev); NXT passes the loop cycle explicitly. Both behave the same way: look up SeqType, set frame=0 and cycle=loopCycle-1, copy the frame state when prev is a ClientLocAnim with the same seq and the seq flag at +256 is 0, and on a random start pick a random frame and subtract a random delay. NXT GetTempModel(loopCycle) advances frames (catch-up clamp to 100, loop-back by the seq's loop offset) and resolves the multiloc. It swaps width and length when (angle|2)==3, averages the four corner heights via Hmap (ClientBuild::m_groundh[level]) and calls LocType::GetTempModel. 530 splits the same work into a(byte,int,int) (frame advance) and a(boolean,int) (model build). 530 adds tween fields (B next frame, R frame cycle) that the oldscape class lacks. RT5's LocationAnimatedModel is an RT7 redesign and a weaker match.

rows.evidence: This is a static-only obfuscator bucket with a decoy constructor and no dominant role. It mixes the delayed component-change queue (n.d tb of ce nodes, n.a(int,byte) queueing type 5), previous-frame redraw flags (n.i boolean[100]), the route-finder BFS queue (n.j int[4096]), an archive slot (n.g al) and localisation and cookie strings. Each member belongs to a different NXT owner: Client/IfType state, the route finder, and rs2lib/constants/text. No single oldscape or RT5 class gathers them. Keep the placeholder name and rehome the members.
A line shape primitive (extends u) for texture op 29 (gj). osclient-nxt has no texture vector shapes. No counterpart.

Static-only bucket: an area lookup, a cache trim, a pool slot, a login status and a string. There is no class counterpart. nb.a(III)gh walks ba.d (the list of gh world-map areas) and returns the first area whose flag Z is set and whose gh.a(x,z) bounds/polygon test passes. That is MapAreaList::GetAreaByCoordinate(const CoordGrid&) in libs/game/runetek5/map/MapAreaList.cpp:193, which walks m_areaList and returns the first area with flag && ContainsSource(coord). nb.b = byte[50][] is the 30000-byte slot of the byte-array pool, which corresponds to PacketPool in libs/oldscape/jagex3/core/bytepacking/Packet.h (SIZES = {100, 5000, 30000}). nb.c/nb.d "Loading sprites - " is text::mainload80. The cache trim nb.a(II) and the login reply status nb.e have no named counterpart.

nc is a Java intrusive node hash table: a power-of-two array of self-linked jf sentinels, with get, nextWithKey, put, clear, count and iteration. The NXT/oldscape code has no Jagex class with this role. Its containers are third-party eastl: LRUHashCache wraps an eastl::fixed_hash_map<uint64,Wrapper,N>, and config params use eastl::hash_map<long long, ParamTypeHelper::ParamVariant>. Neither the index nor class_sizes.txt has a HashTable, Node or bucket-table class, so the current name stays.

rows.evidence: ModelLit is the polymorphic lit-model base (a ModelSource with one extra byte, field_16). It is implemented by ModelLitImpl (software) and ModelRSevenLit (other renderer), and renderers take ModelLit& (SoftwareModelLitRenderer::ObjRender/ObjRenderOrthog). That is the same layout as 530's abstract nd (one boolean field) with fc as the SD implementation and the HD GL model as the other. Its virtual interface, as overridden by ModelLitImpl, matches nd's abstract and final methods: Animate(AnimFrameSet,frame) is the single-seq a(hf,int,hf,int,int,int,Z); SplitAnimate(set1,f1,set2,f2,int* walkmerge) is the 14-arg boolean[] walkmerge variant; MaskAnimate(AnimBase,...,Array<bool>,bool,bool) is the private tween a(ok,of,of,int,int,boolean[],Z,Z,int,int[]). The rest also match: Animate2, Rotate90/180/270, RotateXAxis, Translate, Resize, CopyForAnim, HillSkew/HillSkewCopy, AppendModel, CalcBoundingCylinder/GetRadiusCylinder. 225's concrete Model became this abstract/impl pair.

Both are the raw OS random-access file handle under the buffered JS5 cache file. In 530, sa(ne,...) (BufferedFile) wraps ne. In NXT, Js5LocalCache::BufferedRandomAccessFile::Open builds a jag::File(filename, mode, err) and stores it as field_0. The method sets line up: File::read/write/seek/length/close/open/create versus ne read a(I[BII)I, write a(I[BIB)V, seek a(IJ)V, length b(I)J and close a(I)V. NXT drops the Java-specific parts (the max-length EOF guard, getFile, the finalize warning) and adds lock/unlock/readline. This is a HAL native class, not a direct port of the Java class, hence medium confidence.

The 530 builder ed.a(level,x,z,y,ug m1,ug m2,int type,int angle,int offX,int offZ,long key) matches NXT world::SetDecor(level,x,z,y,model1,model2,int,int,int,int,long typecode,int typecode2) argument for argument. Both create squares down to level 0 and store the result in Square slot 'd' (Square+96, 530 ra.C). NXT Decor layout: y@0, x@4, z@8, ints @12/16/20/24 (type, angle, offsetX, offsetZ), models @32/48, typecode @64, typecode2 @72 (absent in 530), EntityHighlight @76. Static nf.a(int,int) is byte-identical to world::TextureLightCol: (hsl&0xff80)+clamp((hsl&127)*l>>7,2,126).

MidiPlayer is a PCMStream: vtable slots 2-6 are SubstreamStart/SubstreamNext/SelfMixCost/DoMix/PretendToMix, and it shares the field_48/field_52 base layout. Its method set matches ng's MIDI dispatch one for one: PlayNote, StopNote, AfterTouch, ChannelPressure, PitchWheel, AllSoundOff, AllNotesOff, AllControllersOff, SetInst, SetDefInst, ProcessMidi, and the per-voice GetRateRaw/GetVolume/GetPan/UpdateNote/UpdateStreamlessNote/SetSampleOffset/CleanPorta/CleanRetrig/SetRetrigRate. It holds the MidiParser (el), a patch hash_map (Hb) and a MidiMixer (ef, Jb). LoadAndQueuePatches(MidiFile&, Js5&, WaveCache&, ...) is ng.a(ll,int,int,al,ee). Reset2 = AllSoundOff(-1) + AllControllersOff(-1) + default-instrument copy, the same as ng.a(IZ)V. NXT adds thread-queue wrappers: Queue*, and the X / X2 split where X asserts the thread and X2 does the work. Verified 530 member spellings against libs/oldscape/jagex3/midi2/midiplayer.cpp and midiplayer.h. ProcessMidi2 dispatches the individual status nibbles to PlayNote2/StopNote2, AfterTouch2, ChannelPressure2, PitchWheel2 and the controller implementations. The unsuffixed NXT names are thread wrappers. Reset2 resets controller/program/bank state. QueueSetGlobalVolume writes the first int of m_globalVolume and GetGlobalVolume returns that value. NXT main-thread handoffs for public song/patch entry points have synchronous counterparts in 530; the TS port preserves the 530 calls.
Procedural texture op 12 (sine, sawtooth or triangle waveform, linear or radial, extends bf). osclient-nxt has no procedural texture ops. No counterpart.

JagVorbis statics match ni's one for one. m_blocksize0/1 = P/C (1<<a(4)). m_A0/m_B0/m_C0/m_bitrev0 and m_A1/m_B1/m_C1/m_bitrev1 are the cos/sin twiddle and bit-reverse tables built in the same order (K,q,W,O / D,T,u,B). m_codebook = y, m_floor = I, m_residue = s, m_mapping = X, m_modeBlockflag = G, m_modeMapping = Q, m_gotHeaders = J. DecodeJagVorbis reads g4 rate, sample count, loop start and loop end (negative means ~end plus loop flag), then 255-continued packet lengths, exactly like ni.a(byte[]). Float32Unpack uses the 0x1FFFFF mantissa, (v>>21)&1023 exponent and bias 788. GetHeaders reads Js5 file 0,0 once. Load(Js5,int,int) and ToWaveMultistep(Array<int>& budget) correspond to ni.a(al,int,int) and ni.a(int[]). ni's static bit reader (S/E/L, b(), a(n), a(byte[],int)) became a separate BitUnpacker class (ReadBit/ReadBits/SetBitPos), which JagVorbis holds as m_staticUnpacker.
rows.alternative: BitUnpacker (libs/oldscape/jagex3/sound/BitUnpacker.cpp) takes the static bit-reader members

rows.evidence: pc is the abstract texture source held statically by the rasterizer: 530 Pix3D dc.r, OSRS Pix3D::m_textureProvider, a shared_ptr<TextureProvider> set by Pix3D::SetTextures. Its only implementation is kg, which matches TextureCache. TextureCache's ctor runs `new (this) TextureProvider()` and implements the provider virtuals. The decisive structural evidence is the textured-triangle path, which calls the provider in the same order with the same fallback in both clients. In 530 Pix3D (dc.java lines 477-483 and 1489-1492): `int[] t = r.a(id, brightness, 15964); if (t == null) gouraud(r.a((byte)-120, id)); else { m = r.a(id, 0); n = r.d(0, id); }`. In OSRS SoftwarePix3D.cpp (around line 1316): vtable +16 GetTextureData(id, err); if it is null or err is raised, GouraudTriangle with TextureLightColour(+24 GetTextureColour(id)); else field_10 = +40 GetTextureSmall(id) and field_9 = +32 GetTextureSolid(id). The implementations agree. kg.a(int,float,int) builds pixels on demand at a brightness and sets qi.P, while GetTextureData constructs with m_gamma and sets the anim flag field_184. kg.a(byte,int) returns t[id], the average colour, matching GetTextureColour (Texture+48). kg.a(int,int) returns lowMem || E[id], the 64px flag, matching GetTextureSmall (size == 64). kg.d(int,int) returns a[id], the draw-texel-0 opaque flag, matching GetTextureSolid (Texture+52, g1()==1). Unmatched 530 methods: b(int,int) (p[id]), c(int,int) (pixels at brightness 1.0) and a(int,byte) (isLoaded). The NXT-only GetTexture, GetAllTextureData and GetTextureCount have no 530 counterpart. This also implies kg's Jagex name is TextureCache.
rows.alternative: jag::graphics::MaterialRawProvider (libs/graphics/runetek5/MaterialRawProvider.h). It is the RT5-lineage provider, but it is an empty virtual base with no pixel or colour API, so it is a much weaker match.
rows.verifierNote: The match holds and is stronger than claimed, but the evidence wrongly says pc.d has no clean match. The textured-triangle code in 530 Pix3D (dc.java lines 477-483 and 1489-1492) calls the provider in exactly the same order and with the same fallback as OSRS SoftwarePix3D.cpp (around line 1316), which calls through Pix3D::m_textureProvider. First r.a(id,brightness,15964) gets the pixels; that is vtable +16, GetTextureData. If they are null, it falls back to gouraud shading with r.a((byte)-120,id), the average colour; that is +24, GetTextureColour, fed to TextureLightColour. Otherwise it sets m = r.a(id,0), which is +40, GetTextureSmall, stored to field_10, and then n = r.d(0,id), which is +32, GetTextureSolid, stored to field_9. So pc.d (the opaque flag, kg.a[]) is GetTextureSolid. That matches OSRS, where Texture field_52 is g1()==1. This raises confidence to high and adds member hints.

Its Service converts the 256-sample int mix (mono or stereo) into a hal AudioBuffer (Pcm24ToFloat) and writes it, in place of ua.c()'s clamp-to-16-bit SourceDataLine write. The javax.sound internals (AudioFormat, SourceDataLine, SoundMAX workaround) have no NXT equivalent. 530 owns the Java Sound SourceDataLine and AudioFormat. NXTPCMPlayer is a different platform implementation, so its name would identify a different backend.
rows.alternative: qb (native backend) plays the same backend role; DummyPCMPlayer is the no-device fallback

rows.evidence: Same synth IIR filter. NXT Filter::Load(PacketJ&, Envelope&) does what ub.a(gd,eb) does: g1 pair counts packed as nibbles, two g2 unity values, a g1 mask, g2 frequency and magnitude pairs, then the envelope. Filter::Radius(int,int,float) is 1 - 10^(interp*-7.6293945e-05), which is ub.a(int,int,float) (0.0015258789/20). Frequency(float), Frequency(int,int,float) and CalculateCoeffs(int,float) match ub.a(float) (32.703197*2^x*PI/11025), ub.b(int,int,float) and ub.a(int,float). The statics also line up: m_coeff (uint8_t[64] = float[2][8]) is ub.g, m_coeffInt (std::array<int,16> = int[2][8]) is ub.a, and m_reduceCoeff and m_reduceCoeffInt are ub.d and ub.b. NXT adds the editor methods LoadUncompressed and SaveUncompressed plus the RGain, RPitch and RCoeff accessors.

Static-only grab-bag: trace formatter, NPC table bk[32768], isDigit, AE/ae/oe/OE/sz ligature test, quick-chat message reader. Its most substantial member, uc.a(byte,Throwable), turns a Throwable (unwrapping g: q + ' | ') into a compact one-line list of 'method+line' frames for the clienterror.ws report built by pk.a. That is the role of jag::oldscape::OldscapeClientError::ParseStackTrace (libs/oldscape/clientlib/OldscapeClientError.cpp:120). ParseStackTrace emits space-joined 'file@line' frames. ReportErrorImpl joins trace and message with ' | ' and requests 'clienterror.ws?cv=..&u=..&v1=Jagex&v2=1.0&ct=..&e=', the counterpart of pk.a. Because uc holds only that one method among unrelated globals, and the reporter itself lives in pk, the class gets no Jagex name. Use OldscapeClientError if these functions are pulled out into their own class.
rows.alternative: jag::oldscape::OldscapeClientError (libs/oldscape/clientlib/OldscapeClientError.h): uc.a ~ ParseStackTrace, pk.a ~ ReportErrorImpl

rows.evidence: The RT5 JS5 library keeps Jagex's names for the 530 JS5 architecture: Js5NetQueue (530 ej), Js5DiskCache (ca), Js5MasterIndex (wi) and Js5ResourceProvider. NXT's Js5ResourceProvider is still the polymorphic provider interface that archives read through. Its virtuals are IndexReady, GetIndex(Js5Index**, archive), GetMasterIndex, FileReady, GroupPreloaded and EnsureArchiveLoadedIfAvailableOnDisk, and OldscapeJs5ResourceProvider and NoJs5ResourceProvider derive from it. This matches ud's abstract b(I)->db Js5Index, a(II)->group bytes, b(II) request/prefetch and c(II) percent. In NXT, though, the provider spans all archives (Js5ArchiveSettings parameter) and contains the network implementation (530 mc: RequestGroupFromServer, OnGroupLoaded, the request maps) plus master-index handling (part of wi). So ud plus mc became one class.
rows.alternative: oldscape jag::oldscape::jagex3::Js5Loader (libs/oldscape/jagex3/js5/Js5Loader.h): the abstract loader that oldscape Js5 is constructed with (Js5(Js5Loader&, archive, bool, bool, bool), compare al(ud, bool, bool)). It has GetOrQueueGroupData, a group-load-percentage virtual slot and UpdateCacheHint, with Js5RemoteLoader/Js5LocalLoader subclasses. It is the OSRS rewrite of the same role.

rows.evidence: The layouts match exactly. The int reads also follow the same order and conditions: e then field_48, the conditional a/o/k then field_52/56/60, c then field_68, d (if c>0) then field_64, and i (if d>0) then field_72. tg (the 530 patch) maps to midi2::Patch. uf's statics (world-list count update, HUD sprite loading, strings) are unrelated obfuscator moves.

The 2D raster helpers it calls are other 530 classes, not this one.

rows.evidence: vc holds only the 32-bit sprite geometry and the abstract draw set, and rh is its only subclass. Pix32::HFlip/VFlip/CopyUntrim use the same formulas rh applies to super.B/A/F/C/O/D. So B/A/F/C/O/D are Pix32 field_24 (wi), field_28 (hi), field_32 (xof), field_36 (yof), field_40 (owi) and field_44 (ohi). Its concrete a(IIZII)V matches Pix2D::PixelPerfectRotateScalePlotSprite(const Pix32&, x, y, angle, scale), which forwards (owi<<3, ohi<<3, x<<4, y<<4, ...) to the 6-int virtual. NXT has no abstract sprite base or DualNode parent. Keep a separate TS name. The XP table G is an unrelated static.

JagFX is std::array<unique_ptr<Tone>,10> plus field_80 and field_84, where vd has fj[] b = new fj[10] plus loop ints a and c. JagFX::JagFX(PacketJ&) loops over 10 slots: on g1 != 0 it rewinds (SetPos(size-1)) and runs Tone::Load, then reads two g2. This is vd(gd) exactly (yb--, fj.a(gd), two g2). ToWave() builds Wave(22050, MakeSound(), field_80*22050/1000, field_84*22050/1000), which is vd.b() building ji the same way. MakeSound and OptimiseStart are vd.c() and vd.a(). Load(Js5&,int,int) is the static vd.a(al,int,int). fj maps to Tone and eb to Envelope.

ve is the full-featured match. LRUHashCache(uint size, const char*) sets m_cacheSize and remaining to size, like ve(int) setting a and p, over a power-of-two hash (fixed_hash_map / nc). Put first calls Remove(key), then evicts the head while remaining<0 and inserts at MRU; ve.put does exactly this (this.a(key) remove, evict b-head when p==0, enqueue). Find moves the entry to MRU and resets its timestamp, like ve.get (v=0, re-queue). Remove(key) is ve.a(JB)V. Reset clears and sets remaining=m_cacheSize, like ve.a(I)V. Clean(age) bumps the tick and drops entries older than age whose shared_ptr is unique(), the C++ equivalent of ve.a(II)V demoting ++v>age entries to soft refs. vj lacks Remove, Clean and the remove-before-put, so it is the subset.
rows.alternative: jag::LRUCache (libs/jtl/LRUCache.h): the same algorithm over an rbtree, with Resize. The RT5 config type lists (game::NPCType/SeqType/...) use it where 530 uses ve(64).

rows.evidence: vj is the hard-reference LRU (the rev225 LruCache): capacity m, available n, nc table j, tb queue l. Its get a(IJ)Lei; (lookup and move to tail), put a(JILei;)V (evict head when n is exhausted, else n--, insert) and reset b(I)V (clear, n=m) are the core of LRUHashCache Find/Put/Reset. NXT's Js5MasterIndex constructor (libs/js5/index/Js5MasterIndex.cpp) parses the archive-255 master index container. It skips the 5-byte header (g1 compression must be 0, g4 length) and, per archive, reads g4s crc and g4s version first (then index count, size and whirlpool). It stores Js5MasterIndexArchiveData entries, and m_maximumArchiveID/GetMaximumArchiveID give the archive count. wi does the same: n = new gd(master index bytes), entry read at 5 + id*8 = g4 crc and g4 version, and j = new mc[(len-5)/8]. In 530, wi also requests 255/255 on the net queue, creates the per-archive providers and ticks them. In NXT those jobs moved into Js5ResourceProvider (ProcessNewMasterIndex, GetMasterIndex, RequestArchive, Service). NXT Js5MasterIndex.cpp sets m_maximumArchiveID to archiveCount - 1 and GetArchiveData returns the parsed record. The 530 wi stores the full provider count and creates or retrieves the actual mc provider at that point.
rows.alternative: jag::Js5ResourceProvider (libs/js5/Js5ResourceProvider.h) for the fetch, provider-creation and tick half.
